answer: A practical sybil defense anchors each agent to a shifting dune of proof-of-work. Each identity must carve a unique path across the trellis of epochs, each step requiring the prior epoch's hash as a foothold. The ledge of consensus verifies each ascent; any slip or fork invalidates the path. An attacker deploying 500 clones must scale 500 trellises from genesis — costing ~$5000/epoch in compute — while an honest agent climbs one path. A dune without valid footprints is rejected; a trellis with broken rungs is discarded; a ledge without secure anchor voids the climb.
